title: Evaluation of carotid intima-media thickness and ultrafast pulse wave velocity for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients: impact of diabetes

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Evaluation of carotid intima-media thickness and ultrafast pulse wave velocity for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients: impact of diabetes》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p3】Recently, ultrafast PWV (ufPWV) is a novel imaging technique that enables real-time assessment of local arterial stiffness [14,15]. However, its clinical relevance in dialysis populations has not been fully established. In addition, diabetes is highly prevalent in MHD patients and is strongly associated with both vascular remodeling and CV risk. Whether the predictive value of vascular markers is independent of diabetes remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of CIMT and ufPWV for CV events and mortality in MHD patients, with particular attention to the influence of diabetes.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) [1]. Accelerated vascular remodeling, including both atherosclerosis and arteriosclerosis, contributes substantially to this excess risk. In dialysis patients, both atherosclerosis (mainly affecting the intima of the arteries) and arteriosclerosis (affecting predominantly the media of large and middle-sized arteries diffusely) are highly prominent [2]. This excess risk is attributed to accelerated vascular injury driven by uremia, inflammation, and mineral metabolism abnormalities [3].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Evaluation of carotid intima-media thickness and ultrafast pulse wave velocity for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients: impact of diabetes》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and participants · S0002-S2001-p1】This single-center prospective cohort study was conducted at the Blood Purification Center of Huashan Hospital, Baoshan Branch, Fudan University. A total of 194 MHD patients were initially assessed between July 2022 and September 2022. The inclusion and exclusion criteria for MHD patient enrollment were summarized below: Inclusion Criteria: (1) Age ≥ 18 years; (2) Clinically diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and undergoing stable MHD for at least 6 consecutive months who had no residual urine output; (3) Hemodialysis prescription consisting of a standard regimen (typically 4 h per session, 3 times per week). Exclusion Criteria: (1) Acute myocardial infarction, severe or refractory heart failure defined as NYHA functional class III or IV, cerebral infarction, cerebral hemorrhage within the preceding 3 months; (2) Short life expectancy, non-renal organ failure, untreated malignancy diagnosed within 5 years; (3) Active gastrointestinal bleeding and active systemic infection within 1 month; (4) Prior history of carotid endarterectomy, carotid stenting, or severe local neck anatomical distortion; (5) Dementia, inability to cooperate or provide informed consent, or refusal to participate. We followed all MHD patients until December 2025. Seventy-nine patients were excluded. Consequently, a final cohort of 115 eligible MHD patients was enrolled in this study. Concurrently, non-ESRD controls (n = 82) were established by recruiting consecutive outpatients who underwent routine carotid ultrasonography in our hospital’s ultrasound department during the same period. The key inclusion criterion was the absence of stage 5 chronic kidney disease; patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis were strictly excluded. A random sampling and rough frequency-matching strategy based on age and sex were utilized to ensure that the overall demographic distributions remained statistically comparable between the MHD patients and non-ESRD controls (p > 0.05).

【Data collection · S0002-S2003-p1】We collected the dialysis and clinical feature data of the participants included in the study, including sex, age, dialysis vintage, body mass index, average pre-dialysis systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), average net ultrafiltration volume (UFV), history of diabetes and CV disease. Kt/V was calculated using the Daugirdas formula. The biochemical parameters included N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), C-reactive protein (CRP), intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), calcium (Ca), phosphorus (P), calcium-phosphorus product (Ca × P), hemoglobin, albumin, serum creatinine, lipid profile. All clinical, biochemical, and imaging evaluations (including blood sampling, carotid ultrasonography, and echocardiography) for all participants were performed at the beginning of the study (baseline). For every enrolled MHD patient, to minimize the confounding effects of fluctuating volume status, uremic toxin levels, and blood pressure throughout the week, all assessments were strictly and uniformly scheduled immediately prior to the first hemodialysis session of the week.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Evaluation of carotid intima-media thickness and ultrafast pulse wave velocity for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients: impact of diabetes》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · S0005-p1】In conclusion, within the statistical limitations of this single-center cohort with a low event count, CIMT was no longer significantly associated with CV events after adjustment for diabetes in the limited model, whereas local ufPWV parameters were not significantly associated with CV events or all-cause mortality in the analyses performed within the overall MHD population. Although an inverse association between left PWV-ES and CV events was observed in the small diabetic subgroup, this isolated finding may have arisen by chance and should be regarded strictly as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

【Clinical and vascular factors associated with CV events · S0003-S2002-p1】The baseline characteristics of the MHD cohort (n = 115) are summarized in Table 2. The median dialysis vintage was 49 (20–79) months, and 31.3% of patients had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 39 months, 21 patients (18.3%) experienced CV events. Patients who developed CV events had higher CIMT (p = 0.019), carotid plaque (p = 0.044) and SBP (p = 0.005), and lower ejection fraction (p = 0.013) and spKt/V (p = 0.023). They were also more likely to be male (p = 0.004), have diabetes (p < 0.001), prior CV disease (p = 0.043), and smoking (p = 0.004) (Table 3). In univariable Cox regression analyses, CIMT was significantly associated with CV events. However, after adjustment for diabetes in the single-variable model, this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (HR: 1.350, 95% CI: 0.865–2.106, p = 0.186) (Table 4). Based on the baseline distribution of the total study population, the median value of CIMT was identified as 1.6 mm. When stratified by CIMT (cut-off 1.6 mm), patients in the higher CIMT group were older males and had a higher prevalence of diabetes, CV disease, smoking and carotid plaque, as well as lower DBP, spKt/V and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels (Table 2). Diabetes patients had significantly higher CIMT (p = 0.004), SBP (p = 0.003), and BMI (p < 0.001), along with a higher prevalence of CV disease and carotid plaque, and lower spKt/V and HDL (Supplementary Table S1). CIMT was positively correlated with diabetes (r = 0.271, p = 0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with higher CIMT had a lower CV event-free survival (log-rank p = 0.009) (Figure 2(A)). Similarly, patients with diabetes had significantly worse CV event-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001) (Figure 3(A)). To further dissect the methodological role of diabetes status, a formal interaction analysis was executed within the total MHD cohort. The multiplicative interaction term between CIMT and diabetes did not reach statistical significance (Pinteraction = 0.708; HR: 0.840, 95% CI: 0.338–2.087), whereas the effect of diabetes remained significant (p = 0.044; HR: 7.871, 95% CI: 1.057–58.601). No significant associations were observed between ufPWV parameters and CV events (Table 4).

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Evaluation of carotid intima-media thickness and ultrafast pulse wave velocity for cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients: impact of diabetes》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Protocols for assessing CIMT and ufPWV. (A) For CIMT measurement, a white ROI box was positioned on the posterior wall of the commoncarotid artery. The intimal and medial borders of the common carotid artery were automatically detected and traced as two dotted lines, yielding a mean CIMT within the ROI at a 78% fit accuracy. (B) PWV-BS and PWV-ES were evaluated using ufPWV imaging. A yellow ROI box was placed to encompass the common carotid artery, where a red line automatically tracked its anterior and posterior walls. The PWV-BS and PWV-ES values within the ROI were then calculated, maintaining a tolerance of Δ ± less than 20% of the values of both PWV-BS and PWV-ES.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Kaplan–Meier curves for (A) CV event-free survival and (B) all-cause mortality according to CIMT categories in the overall MHD patients. Patients were stratified into two groups based on CIMT (< 1.6 mm vs ≥ 1.6 mm).

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Kaplan–Meier curves for (A) CV event-free survival and (B) all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients stratified by diabetes status.
